full_judgment: 3. The petitioners' case is that they had their ancestral home on 2.65 acres out of a total of 5.80 acres of Khatian No. 1358 of mouzaMoulvi Bazar Town which comprises several houses, tank, graveyard, gardens etc. wherein the petitioners have been living for generations now. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali, his six brothers, two sisters and mother mutated their names in respect of the entire land of 5.80 acres of the above khatian No. 1358 on the basis of a registered Kabala No. 5879 executed and registered on 31.10.55 by one Keramat Ali in favour of Syed Ashraf Ali, deceased father of the said respondent No.4. The said Keramat Ali auction purchased the entire land of 5.80 acres of the said khatian No. 1358 on 25.9.54 for arrears of rent. The auction purchaser Keramat Ali however sold only 3.15 acres of the khatian land out of 5.80 acres to late Syed Ashraf Ali, father of the respondent No.4. The balance 2.65 acres of ancestral homestead continued to remain in the possession of the petitioners and their predecessors. The predecessors of the petitioners obtained a registered Muktipatra dated 8.5.79 from one of the sons of auction purchaser Keramat Ali, namely HabiburRahman. Thereafter the predecessors of the petitioners by executing and registering three separate deeds of gift, all dated 5.11.78, transferred their right, title and interest in the case land to the petitioners and delivered physical possession thereof to them. The petitioners thereafter instituted Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979 be- fore the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar. After compliance of necessary formalities all the three mutation cases were allowed vide order dated 13.11.79. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali and his 5 brothers filed an objection petition before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1979 was started. The par- ties were notified. After hearing the parties the Circle Officer forwarded the case record to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet for necessary action with a detailed report as he found the case to be complicated. Then the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Additional Deputy Com- missioner (Revenue), Sylhet under section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, shortly the Act, against the Order dated 13.11.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Mutation Appeal Case No. 24 of 1979- 80 was started and the petitioners were notified. By his order dated 10.9.80 the Additional Deputy Com- missioner, Sylhet after hearing the parties rejected the appeal of the respondent No.4 and upheld the or- der dated 13.1l.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar in Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979. Against the aforesaid order of the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Com- missioner, Chittagong Division being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 223 of 1980 under section 147 of the Act which was heard and disposed of by the Additional Commissioner, Chittagong Division by his order dated 15.12.82 dismissing the same and con-firming the order dated 10.9.80 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet.
